note: Create the trigger function that keeps amount and total equal on every insert/update, whichever of the two the writer sets (old app writes amount, new app writes total).

Add nullable column total numeric(10,2) (metadata-only, no rewrite) and the sync trigger in one transaction, so every row written from now on has total. The lock is taken with a 200 ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind it for long.
Backfill total = amount for ids 1..1,000,000 in 250k-row batches, each committed on its own (row locks only; the app never updates existing orders).
Vacuum so the dead row versions from the backfill are reused instead of bloating the table.
Backfill whatever is left above id 10,000,000 (orders inserted before the trigger existed; later ones already have total).
Add CHECK (total IS NOT NULL) as NOT VALID: brief lock, no scan, retried on lock timeout.
Validate the check: a full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes. Fails (and stops the plan) if any row still has a NULL total.
SET NOT NULL on total (Postgres proves it from the validated check, so no scan), then drop the redundant check. Brief lock, retried.
Verify every row has total = amount before switching the app; stops the plan if not.

Roll the app over to read and write total. While old pods (amount) and new pods (total) coexist during the rolling update, the trigger fills whichever column a writer leaves out, so both stay correct.
